sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu nihate sainye tāv ubhau yuddhadurmadau saṃgrāme vyavatiṣṭhetāṃ yathā vai vṛtravāsavau
english: When that host had been slain, those two, both maddened with the lust of battle, stood facing each other in the fray, even as Vṛtra and Vāsava of old.

sanskrit: ādravantam abhiprekṣya rākṣasaṃ yuddhadurmadam irāvān krodhasaṃrabdhaḥ pratyadhāvan mahābalaḥ
english: Beholding the rākṣasa, frenzied for combat, rushing upon him, the mighty Irāvān, inflamed with wrath, charged against him in turn.

sanskrit: samabhyāśagatasyājau tasya khaḍgena durmateḥ ciccheda kārmukaṃ dīptaṃ śarāvāpaṃ ca pañcakam
english: As the evil-minded one drew near in the battle, with his sword he cut asunder his blazing bow and his five quivers as well.

sanskrit: sa nikṛttaṃ dhanur dṛṣṭvā khaṃ javena samāviśat irāvantam abhikruddhaṃ mohayann iva māyayā
english: Seeing his bow cut through, he sprang swiftly into the sky, as though to bewilder the enraged Irāvān by his magic.

sanskrit: tato 'ntarikṣam utpatya irāvān api rākṣasam vimohayitvā māyābhis tasya gātrāṇi sāyakaiḥ ciccheda sarvamarmajñaḥ kāmarūpo durāsadaḥ
english: Then Irāvān too, leaping into the firmament, baffled the rākṣasa with his own illusions; and that one, knower of every vital point, able to take any form at will and hard to assail, cut the other's limbs to pieces with his shafts.

sanskrit: tathā sa rākṣasaśreṣṭhaḥ śaraiḥ kṛttaḥ punaḥ punaḥ saṃbabhūva mahārāja samavāpa ca yauvanam
english: Yet that foremost of rākṣasas, though hewn by the arrows again and again, knit himself whole once more, O great king, and recovered his youth.

sanskrit: māyā hi sahajā teṣāṃ vayo rūpaṃ ca kāmajam evaṃ tad rākṣasasyāṅgaṃ chinnaṃ chinnaṃ vyarohata
english: For illusion is inborn in their kind, and their age and form are shaped by will; thus the rākṣasa's body, severed and severed again, grew back each time.

sanskrit: irāvān api saṃkruddho rākṣasaṃ taṃ mahābalam paraśvadhena tīkṣṇena ciccheda ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: Irāvān too, exceedingly wroth, hewed that mighty rākṣasa again and again with a keen battle-axe.

sanskrit: sa tena balinā vīraś chidyamāna iva drumaḥ rākṣaso vyanadad ghoraṃ sa śabdas tumulo 'bhavat
english: Cleft by that strong hero like a tree under the axe, the rākṣasa roared horribly, and that cry grew into a tumult.

sanskrit: paraśvadhakṣataṃ rakṣaḥ susrāva rudhiraṃ bahu tataś cukrodha balavāṃś cakre vegaṃ ca saṃyuge
english: Gashed by the battle-axe, the rākṣasa streamed with abundant blood; thereupon the strong one fell into a fury and put forth his utmost speed in the encounter.

sanskrit: ārśyaśṛṅgis tato dṛṣṭvā samare śatrum ūrjitam kṛtvā ghoraṃ mahad rūpaṃ grahītum upacakrame saṃgrāmaśiraso madhye sarveṣāṃ tatra paśyatām
english: Then the son of Ṛśyaśṛṅga, beholding his foe grown mighty in the fight, assumed a huge and dreadful shape and set about seizing him, there in the very midst of the battle-front, while all looked on.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśīṃ māyāṃ rākṣasasya mahātmanaḥ irāvān api saṃkruddho māyāṃ sraṣṭuṃ pracakrame
english: Beholding that illusion of the great-souled rākṣasa, Irāvān too, sore enraged, set about conjuring an illusion of his own.

sanskrit: tasya krodhābhibhūtasya saṃyugeṣv anivartinaḥ yo 'nvayo mātṛkas tasya sa enam abhipedivān
english: As he, overmastered by wrath and never turning back in battles, stood there, the kindred of his mother's line came to his aid.

sanskrit: sa nāgair bahuśo rājan sarvataḥ saṃvṛto raṇe dadhāra sumahad rūpam ananta iva bhogavān tato bahuvidhair nāgaiś chādayām āsa rākṣasam
english: Encompassed on every side in the fray by a host of serpents, O king, he took on a vast form, like Ananta wreathed in his coils, and then with snakes of many kinds he covered over the rākṣasa.

sanskrit: chādyamānas tu nāgaiḥ sa dhyātvā rākṣasapuṃgavaḥ sauparṇaṃ rūpam āsthāya bhakṣayām āsa pannagān
english: But that bull among rākṣasas, while being mantled by the serpents, bethought himself, took the form of Suparṇa, and devoured the snakes.

sanskrit: māyayā bhakṣite tasminn anvaye tasya mātṛke vimohitam irāvantam asinā rākṣaso 'vadhīt
english: When by that magic the kindred of his mother's line had been consumed, the rākṣasa, finding Irāvān bewildered, slew him with his sword.

sanskrit: sakuṇḍalaṃ samukuṭaṃ padmendusadṛśaprabham irāvataḥ śiro rakṣaḥ pātayām āsa bhūtale
english: The head of Irāvān, with its earrings and diadem, gleaming like the lotus and the moon, the rākṣasa struck down to the earth.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu nihate vīre rākṣasenārjunātmaje viśokāḥ samapadyanta dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ sarājakāḥ
english: When that hero, Arjuna's son, had been slain by the rākṣasa, the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, together with their king, were freed of their grief.

sanskrit: tasmin mahati saṃgrāme tādṛśe bhairave punaḥ mahān vyatikaro ghoraḥ senayoḥ samapadyata
english: In that great and terrible battle, once again a fearful and grievous confusion arose between the two armies.

sanskrit: hayā gajāḥ padātāś ca vimiśrā dantibhir hatāḥ rathāś ca dantinaś caiva pattibhis tatra sūditāḥ
english: Horses, elephants, and foot-soldiers, all confounded together, were slain by the tuskers; and chariots and elephants too were destroyed there by the infantry.

sanskrit: tathā pattirathaughāś ca hayāś ca bahavo raṇe rathibhir nihatā rājaṃs tava teṣāṃ ca saṃkule
english: And in the press of battle great masses of foot and chariots and many horses, O king, were slain by the chariot-warriors of thine and theirs alike.

sanskrit: ajānann arjunaś cāpi nihataṃ putram aurasam jaghāna samare śūrān rājñas tān bhīṣmarakṣiṇaḥ
english: Arjuna too, not knowing that his own begotten son was slain, struck down in the battle those heroic kings who guarded Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: tathaiva tāvakā rājan sṛñjayāś ca mahābalāḥ juhvataḥ samare prāṇān nijaghnur itaretaram
english: In like manner thy warriors, O king, and the mighty Sṛñjayas, offering up their very lives in the fight, slew one another.

sanskrit: muktakeśā vikavacā virathāś chinnakārmukāḥ bāhubhiḥ samayudhyanta samavetāḥ parasparam
english: With their hair loosened, stripped of their armour, robbed of their chariots, their bows cut asunder, they grappled hand to hand, closing with one another.

sanskrit: tathā marmātigair bhīṣmo nijaghāna mahārathān kampayan samare senāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahābalaḥ
english: And Bhīṣma, with shafts that pierced the vital parts, struck down great chariot-warriors, the mighty one making the army of the Pāṇḍavas tremble in the fray.

sanskrit: tena yaudhiṣṭhire sainye bahavo mānavā hatāḥ dantinaḥ sādinaś caiva rathino 'tha hayās tathā
english: By him in Yudhiṣṭhira's host were many men slain — elephants and horsemen and chariot-fighters and horses as well.

sanskrit: tatra bhārata bhīṣmasya raṇe dṛṣṭvā parākramam atyadbhutam apaśyāma śakrasyeva parākramam
english: There, O Bhārata, beholding the prowess of Bhīṣma in the battle, we saw it most marvellous, like the prowess of Śakra himself.

sanskrit: tathaiva bhīmasenasya pārṣatasya ca bhārata raudram āsīt tadā yuddhaṃ sātvatasya ca dhanvinaḥ
english: In like manner, O Bhārata, fierce was then the battle of Bhīmasena and of the son of Pṛṣata and of the bowman of the Sātvata line.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā droṇasya vikrāntaṃ pāṇḍavān bhayam āviśat eka eva raṇe śakto hantum asmān sasainikān
english: Beholding the valour of Droṇa, fear entered the Pāṇḍavas: 'He alone in battle is able to slay us together with our hosts.'

sanskrit: kiṃ punaḥ pṛthivīśūrair yodhavrātaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ ity abruvan mahārāja raṇe droṇena pīḍitāḥ
english: 'How much more, then, when he is ringed about by the heroes of the earth and bands of warriors?' — thus they spoke, O great king, hard-pressed by Droṇa in the fight.

sanskrit: vartamāne tathā raudre saṃgrāme bharatarṣabha ubhayoḥ senayoḥ śūrā nāmṛṣyanta parasparam
english: As that fearful battle thus raged on, O bull of the Bharatas, the heroes of both armies brooked no quarter from one another.

sanskrit: āviṣṭā iva yudhyante rakṣobhūtā mahābalāḥ tāvakāḥ pāṇḍaveyāś ca saṃrabdhās tāta dhanvinaḥ
english: As though possessed, the mighty bowmen fought, become very rākṣasas — thy men and the sons of Pāṇḍu alike, O sire, all in a frenzy.

sanskrit: na sma paśyāmahe kaṃ cid yaḥ prāṇān parirakṣati saṃgrāme daityasaṃkāśe tasmin yoddhā narādhipa
english: We saw not a single warrior, O lord of men, who sought to guard his own life in that battle that resembled a war of the Daityas.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca irāvantaṃ tu nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā pārthā mahārathāḥ saṃgrāme kim akurvanta tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When they saw Irāvān slain, what did the sons of Pṛthā, those great chariot-warriors, do in the battle? Tell me that, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca irāvantaṃ tu nihataṃ saṃgrāme vīkṣya rākṣasaḥ vyanadat sumahānādaṃ bhaimasenir ghaṭotkacaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing Irāvān slain in the battle, the rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca, son of Bhīmasena, sent forth a mighty roar.

sanskrit: nadatas tasya śabdena pṛthivī sāgarāmbarā saparvatavanā rājaṃś cacāla subhṛśaṃ tadā antarikṣaṃ diśaś caiva sarvāś ca pradiśas tathā
english: At the sound of his roaring, the earth, robed in her oceans and clad in her mountains and forests, shook violently then, O king, and so too the firmament, all the quarters, and the intermediate points.

sanskrit: taṃ śrutvā sumahānādaṃ tava sainyasya bhārata ūrustambhaḥ samabhavad vepathuḥ sveda eva ca
english: Hearing that mighty roar, O Bhārata, in thy army there arose a stiffening of the thighs, a trembling, and a breaking out of sweat.

sanskrit: sarva eva ca rājendra tāvakā dīnacetasaḥ sarpavat samaveṣṭanta siṃhabhītā gajā iva
english: And all thy men, O lord of kings, downcast in spirit, coiled in upon themselves like snakes, like elephants in dread of the lion.

sanskrit: ninadat sumahānādaṃ nirghātam iva rākṣasaḥ jvalitaṃ śūlam udyamya rūpaṃ kṛtvā vibhīṣaṇam
english: Roaring his mighty roar like a thunderclap, the rākṣasa, lifting on high his blazing spear, assumed a terrifying shape.

sanskrit: nānāpraharaṇair ghorair vṛto rākṣasapuṃgavaiḥ ājagāma susaṃkruddhaḥ kālāntakayamopamaḥ
english: Surrounded by bulls among rākṣasas armed with dreadful weapons of every kind, he came on in fury, like Yama the all-ending Death.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya saṃkruddhaṃ bhīmadarśanam svabalaṃ ca bhayāt tasya prāyaśo vimukhīkṛtam
english: Beholding him bearing down, wrathful and terrible to look upon, and seeing his own host for the most part turned away in fear of him —

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā ghaṭotkacam upādravat pragṛhya vipulaṃ cāpaṃ siṃhavad vinadan muhuḥ
english: Then king Duryodhana rushed upon Ghaṭotkaca, grasping his great bow and roaring again and again like a lion.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhato 'nuyayau cainaṃ sravadbhiḥ parvatopamaiḥ kuñjarair daśasāhasrair vaṅgānām adhipaḥ svayam
english: And behind him there followed the lord of the Vaṅgas himself, with ten thousand elephants, mountain-like and streaming with rut.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya gajānīkena saṃvṛtam putraṃ tava mahārāja cukopa sa niśācaraḥ
english: Beholding thy son bearing down upon him, hedged about by that array of elephants, O great king, the night-ranger flew into a rage.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam rākṣasānāṃ ca rājendra duryodhanabalasya ca
english: Then began a battle, tumultuous and making the hair stand on end, O lord of kings, between the rākṣasas and the host of Duryodhana.

sanskrit: gajānīkaṃ ca saṃprekṣya meghavṛndam ivodyatam abhyadhāvanta saṃkruddhā rākṣasāḥ śastrapāṇayaḥ
english: And beholding the elephant-array rising up like a bank of clouds, the rākṣasas, weapons in hand, charged at it in fury.

sanskrit: nadanto vividhān nādān meghā iva savidyutaḥ śaraśaktyṛṣṭinārācair nighnanto gajayodhinaḥ
english: Sounding forth divers cries, like thunderclouds charged with lightning, they smote the elephant-riders with arrows, darts, lances, and iron shafts.

sanskrit: bhiṇḍipālais tathā śūlair mudgaraiḥ saparaśvadhaiḥ parvatāgraiś ca vṛkṣaiś ca nijaghnus te mahāgajān
english: With bhiṇḍipālas and spears, with maces and battle-axes, with mountain-peaks and trees, they struck down the great elephants.

sanskrit: bhinnakumbhān virudhirān bhinnagātrāṃś ca vāraṇān apaśyāma mahārāja vadhyamānān niśācaraiḥ
english: Elephants with their frontal globes split, bathed in blood, their bodies torn open, we beheld, O great king, being slaughtered by the night-rangers.

sanskrit: teṣu prakṣīyamāṇeṣu bhagneṣu gajayodhiṣu duryodhano mahārāja rākṣasān samupādravat
english: As those elephant-warriors were being destroyed and broken, Duryodhana, O great king, rushed upon the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: amarṣavaśam āpannas tyaktvā jīvitam ātmanaḥ mumoca niśitān bāṇān rākṣaseṣu mahābalaḥ
english: Yielding himself to wrath and setting his own life at naught, the mighty one loosed sharpened arrows upon the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: jaghāna ca maheṣvāsaḥ pradhānāṃs tatra rākṣasān saṃkruddho bharataśreṣṭha putro duryodhanas tava
english: And that great bowman, thy son Duryodhana, O foremost of the Bharatas, in his fury slew the chief rākṣasas there.

sanskrit: vegavantaṃ mahāraudraṃ vidyujjihvaṃ pramāthinam śaraiś caturbhiś caturo nijaghāna mahārathaḥ
english: That great chariot-warrior slew with four arrows four of them — the swift, the most fearsome, Vidyujjihvā, and Pramāthin.

sanskrit: tataḥ punar ameyātmā śaravarṣaṃ durāsadam mumoca bharataśreṣṭha niśācarabalaṃ prati
english: Then again that one of immeasurable spirit, O foremost of the Bharatas, loosed an irresistible torrent of arrows against the host of the night-rangers.

sanskrit: tat tu dṛṣṭvā mahat karma putrasya tava māriṣa krodhenābhiprajajvāla bhaimasenir mahābalaḥ
english: Beholding that great deed of thy son, O honoured one, the mighty Ghaṭotkaca, son of Bhīmasena, blazed up with wrath.

sanskrit: visphārya ca mahac cāpam indrāśanisamasvanam abhidudrāva vegena duryodhanam ariṃdamam
english: And twanging his great bow, whose sound was like the thunderbolt of Indra, he rushed with speed upon Duryodhana, that crusher of foes.

sanskrit: tam āpatantam udvīkṣya kālasṛṣṭam ivāntakam na vivyathe mahārāja putro duryodhanas tava
english: Beholding him bearing down like Death let loose by Time, thy son Duryodhana, O great king, faltered not at all.

sanskrit: athainam abravīt kruddhaḥ krūraḥ saṃraktalocanaḥ ye tvayā sunṛśaṃsena dīrghakālaṃ pravāsitāḥ yac ca te pāṇḍavā rājaṃś chaladyūte parājitāḥ
english: Then the cruel one, enraged, his eyes red with anger, spoke to him: 'Those whom thou, most ruthless, didst banish into exile for a long while — those Pāṇḍavas, O king, whom thou didst vanquish by fraud at the game of dice —'

sanskrit: yac caiva draupadī kṛṣṇā ekavastrā rajasvalā sabhām ānīya durbuddhe bahudhā kleśitā tvayā
english: '— and when Draupadī Kṛṣṇā, clad in a single garment, in her courses, was dragged into the assembly hall, O evil-minded one, and by thee tormented in many ways —'

sanskrit: tava ca priyakāmena āśramasthā durātmanā saindhavena parikliṣṭā paribhūya pitṝn mama
english: '— and how, to do thee a pleasure, the vile lord of the Sindhus, while she dwelt in the hermitage, harassed her, setting at naught my elders —'

sanskrit: eteṣām avamānānām anyeṣāṃ ca kulādhama antam adya gamiṣyāmi yadi notsṛjase raṇam
english: '— of these affronts, O basest of thy line, and of the others too, this day I shall make an end, unless thou quit the battle.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu haiḍimbo mahad visphārya kārmukam saṃdaśya daśanair oṣṭhaṃ sṛkkiṇī parisaṃlihan
english: Having spoken thus, the son of Hiḍimbā, twanging his great bow, biting his lip with his teeth and licking the corners of his mouth —

sanskrit: śaravarṣeṇa mahatā duryodhanam avākirat parvataṃ vāridhārābhiḥ prāvṛṣīva balāhakaḥ
english: — overwhelmed Duryodhana with a mighty rain of arrows, as a storm-cloud in the rains drenches a mountain with its torrents of water.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tatas tad bāṇavarṣaṃ tu duḥsahaṃ dānavair api dadhāra yudhi rājendro yathā varṣaṃ mahādvipaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then that shower of arrows, unbearable even to the Dānavas, the lord of kings sustained in the battle, as a great elephant withstands the downpour of rain.

sanskrit: tataḥ krodhasamāviṣṭo niḥśvasann iva pannagaḥ saṃśayaṃ paramaṃ prāptaḥ putras te bharatarṣabha
english: Then, filled with wrath, hissing like a serpent, thy son, O bull of the Bharatas, came into the utmost peril.

sanskrit: mumoca niśitāṃs tīkṣṇān nārācān pañcaviṃśatim te 'patan sahasā rājaṃs tasmin rākṣasapuṃgave āśīviṣā iva kruddhāḥ parvate gandhamādane
english: He loosed five-and-twenty whetted, keen iron shafts; and they fell all at once, O king, upon that bull among rākṣasas, like wrathful venom-fanged serpents upon the mountain Gandhamādana.

sanskrit: sa tair viddhaḥ sravan raktaṃ prabhinna iva kuñjaraḥ dadhre matiṃ vināśāya rājñaḥ sa piśitāśanaḥ jagrāha ca mahāśaktiṃ girīṇām api dāraṇīm
english: Pierced by them and streaming with blood like an elephant in rut, that eater of flesh set his mind upon the king's destruction and grasped a great dart, able to rend even the mountains.

sanskrit: saṃpradīptāṃ maholkābhām aśanīṃ maghavān iva samudyacchan mahābāhur jighāṃsus tanayaṃ tava
english: Flaming like a great meteor, that dart the mighty-armed one raised on high, as Maghavan his thunderbolt, eager to slay thy son.

sanskrit: tām udyatām abhiprekṣya vaṅgānām adhipas tvaran kuñjaraṃ girisaṃkāśaṃ rākṣasaṃ pratyacodayat
english: Seeing it lifted up, the lord of the Vaṅgas, in haste, urged on against the rākṣasa his elephant, huge as a hill.

sanskrit: sa nāgapravareṇājau balinā śīghragāminā yato duryodhanarathas taṃ mārgaṃ pratyapadyata rathaṃ ca vārayām āsa kuñjareṇa sutasya te
english: With that strong and swift-footed prince of elephants, in the battle, he made for the path where Duryodhana's chariot stood, and with the tusker barred the way of thy son's car.

sanskrit: mārgam āvāritaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājñā vaṅgena dhīmatā ghaṭotkaco mahārāja krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ udyatāṃ tāṃ mahāśaktiṃ tasmiṃś cikṣepa vāraṇe
english: Seeing his path blocked by the wise king of the Vaṅgas, Ghaṭotkaca, O great king, his eyes red with wrath, hurled that uplifted great dart at the elephant.

sanskrit: sa tayābhihato rājaṃs tena bāhuvimuktayā saṃjātarudhirotpīḍaḥ papāta ca mamāra ca
english: Struck by it, O king, as it sped from his arm, the elephant, with a gush of welling blood, fell down and died.

sanskrit: pataty atha gaje cāpi vaṅgānām īśvaro balī javena samabhidrutya jagāma dharaṇītalam
english: And as the elephant fell, the strong lord of the Vaṅgas, springing down with speed, came to the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: duryodhano 'pi saṃprekṣya pātitaṃ varavāraṇam prabhagnaṃ ca balaṃ dṛṣṭvā jagāma paramāṃ vyathām
english: Duryodhana too, beholding that noble elephant struck down, and seeing his host broken, fell into the deepest distress.

sanskrit: kṣatradharmaṃ puraskṛtya ātmanaś cābhimānitām prāpte 'pakramaṇe rājā tasthau girir ivācalaḥ
english: Yet setting before him the law of the warrior and his own self-respect, the king, though the hour to retreat had come, stood firm as an unshaken mountain.

sanskrit: saṃdhāya ca śitaṃ bāṇaṃ kālāgnisamatejasam mumoca paramakruddhas tasmin ghore niśācare
english: And fitting to his bow a sharpened arrow, blazing like the fire of Time, in utmost wrath he loosed it at that dreadful night-ranger.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya bāṇam indrāśaniprabham lāghavād vañcayām āsa mahākāyo ghaṭotkacaḥ
english: Beholding that arrow speeding on, bright as Indra's thunderbolt, the huge-bodied Ghaṭotkaca by his nimbleness eluded it.

sanskrit: bhūya eva nanādograḥ krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ trāsayan sarvabhūtāni yugānte jalado yathā
english: Once more the fierce one roared, his eyes red with wrath, affrighting all beings, like a thunder-cloud at the ending of an age.

sanskrit: taṃ śrutvā ninadaṃ ghoraṃ tasya bhīṣmasya rakṣasaḥ ācāryam upasaṃgamya bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo 'bravīt
english: Hearing that dreadful roar of the rākṣasa, Bhīṣma, the son of Śaṃtanu, drew near to the preceptor and spoke:

sanskrit: yathaiṣa ninado ghoraḥ śrūyate rākṣaseritaḥ haiḍimbo yudhyate nūnaṃ rājñā duryodhanena ha
english: 'By the dreadful roar that is heard, raised by the rākṣasa, surely the son of Hiḍimbā is even now doing battle with king Duryodhana.'
